data\\ndata: {\\\"title\\\":\\\"Models\\\",\\\"description\\\":\\\"Choose and configure language models for your agents\\\",\\\"url\\\":\\\"https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"# Models\\\\n\\\\nEvery Agent ultimately calls an LLM. The SDK abstracts models behind two lightweight interfaces:\\\\n\\\\n*   [`Model`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/interfaces/model) – knows how to make _one_ request against a specific API.\\\\n*   [`ModelProvider`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/interfaces/modelprovider) – resolves human‑readable model **names** (e.g. `'gpt-5.6-sol'`) to `Model` instances.\\\\n\\\\nIn day‑to‑day work you normally only interact with model **names** and occasionally `ModelSettings`.\\\\n\\\\nSpecifying a model per‑agent\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Agent } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nconst agent = new Agent({  name: 'Creative writer',  model: 'gpt-5.6-sol',});\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Choosing models\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Choosing models”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#choosing-models)\\\\n\\\\n### Default model\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Default model”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#default-model)\\\\n\\\\nWhen you don’t specify a model when initializing an `Agent`, the default model will be used. The default is currently [`gpt-5.6-luna`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna) with `reasoning.effort: \\\\\\\"none\\\\\\\"` and `text.verbosity: \\\\\\\"low\\\\\\\"` for efficient, high-volume agent workloads.\\\\n\\\\nIf you want to switch to another model like `gpt-5.6-sol`, there are two ways to configure your agents.\\\\n\\\\nFirst, if you want to consistently use a specific model for all agents that do not set a custom model, set the `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL` environment variable before running your agents.\\\\n\\\\nTerminal window\\\\n\\\\n`export OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-5.6-solnode my-awesome-agent.js`\\\\n\\\\nSecond, you can set a default model for a `Runner` instance. If you don’t set a model for an agent, this `Runner`’s default model will be used.\\\\n\\\\nSet a default model for a Runner\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Runner } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nconst runner = new Runner({ model: 'gpt-4.1-mini' });\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n#### GPT-5.x models\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “GPT-5.x models”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#gpt-5x-models)\\\\n\\\\nWhen you use any GPT-5.x model such as [`gpt-5.6-sol`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol) in this way, the SDK applies default `modelSettings`. It sets the ones that work the best for most use cases. To adjust the reasoning effort for the default model, pass your own `modelSettings`:\\\\n\\\\nCustomize GPT-5 default settings\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Agent } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nconst myAgent = new Agent({  name: 'My Agent',  instructions: \\\\\\\"You're a helpful agent.\\\\\\\",  // If OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol is set, passing only modelSettings works.  // It's also fine to pass a GPT-5.x model name explicitly:  model: 'gpt-5.6-sol',  modelSettings: {    reasoning: { effort: 'high' },    text: { verbosity: 'low' },  },});\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nIf latency and cost matter, start with the default `gpt-5.6-luna` configuration or use `reasoning.effort: \\\\\\\"none\\\\\\\"` on another GPT-5.x model, then increase reasoning effort only if your task needs more deliberate reasoning.\\\\n\\\\n#### Non-GPT-5 models\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Non-GPT-5 models”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#non-gpt-5-models)\\\\n\\\\nIf you pass a non–GPT-5 model name without custom `modelSettings`, the SDK reverts to generic `modelSettings` compatible with any model.\\\\n\\\\n* * *\\\\n\\\\n## OpenAI provider configuration\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “OpenAI provider configuration”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#openai-provider-configuration)\\\\n\\\\n### The OpenAI provider\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “The OpenAI provider”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#the-openai-provider)\\\\n\\\\nThe default `ModelProvider` resolves names using the OpenAI APIs. It supports two distinct endpoints:\\\\n\\\\n| API | Usage | Call `setOpenAIAPI()` |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| Chat Completions | Standard chat & function calls | `setOpenAIAPI('chat_completions')` |\\\\n| Responses | New streaming‑first generative API (tool calls, flexible outputs) | `setOpenAIAPI('responses')`_(default)_ |\\\\n\\\\n#### Authentication\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Authentication”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#authentication)\\\\n\\\\nSet default OpenAI key\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { setDefaultOpenAIKey } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nsetDefaultOpenAIKey(process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY!); // sk-...\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nYou can also plug your own `OpenAI` client via `setDefaultOpenAIClient(client)` if you need custom networking settings. Directly supplied clients must use `openai` 7.2 or later.\\\\n\\\\n#### Provider options reference\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Provider options reference”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#provider-options-reference)\\\\n\\\\nWhen you instantiate `OpenAIProvider` directly, these options control client construction, endpoint selection, and feature validation:\\\\n\\\\n| Option | Purpose |\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\n| `apiKey` | API key used when the provider creates its own OpenAI client. Defaults to the SDK-wide OpenAI key. |\\\\n| `baseURL` | HTTP base URL for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Cannot be combined with `openAIClient`. |\\\\n| `websocketBaseURL` | WebSocket base URL for Responses WebSocket transport. Cannot be combined with `openAIClient`. |\\\\n| `openAIClient` | Preconfigured client from `openai` 7.2 or later. Cannot be combined with `apiKey`, `baseURL`, or `websocketBaseURL`. |\\\\n| `organization` / `project` | Organization and project values passed when the provider creates its own OpenAI client. |\\\\n| `useResponses` | Select the Responses API (`true`) or Chat Completions API (`false`) for string model names resolved by this provider. Defaults to the process-wide `setOpenAIAPI(...)` setting. |\\\\n| `useResponsesWebSocket` | Use the WebSocket transport for Responses models resolved by this provider. Defaults to the process-wide `setOpenAIResponsesTransport(...)` setting. |\\\\n| `cacheResponsesWebSocketModels` | Reuse websocket-backed Responses model wrappers for connection reuse. Defaults to `true`; call `provider.close()` during shutdown to close cached wrappers. |\\\\n| `responsesWebSocketOptions` | Configure client keepalive with `pingIntervalMs` and `pingTimeoutMs`. |\\\\n| `strictFeatureValidation` | For Chat Completions models, raise `UserError` for Responses-only features such as `previousResponseId`, `conversationId`, `prompt`, and assistant message phases. By default those features are warned and ignored. |\\\\n\\\\nWhen a Responses assistant message includes a `phase` of `commentary` or `final_answer`, the SDK preserves it as a top-level field on the history item. That phase survives session replay through `OpenAIConversationsSession` and serialized `RunState`. Chat Completions has no equivalent field, so it warns and drops the phase by default; set `strictFeatureValidation: true` to reject that conversion instead.\\\\n\\\\n#### Chat Completions audio\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Chat Completions audio”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#chat-completions-audio)\\\\n\\\\nAudio-capable Chat Completions models accept endpoint-specific `modalities` and `audio` request fields through `modelSettings.providerData`. Use an audio-capable model and follow the official [Audio and speech guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/audio#add-audio-to-your-existing-application) for supported request values.\\\\n\\\\nBoth non-streamed and streamed calls preserve audio-only assistant output. The normalized `ModelResponse.output` contains an `audio` content part. When that message becomes a run item, `RunMessageOutputItem.rawItem` contains the same part. Its `audio` field contains the base64 data, while `providerData` retains provider metadata such as `id`, `transcript`, `format`, and `expires_at`. When the same choice also contains text or a refusal, the normalized assistant message keeps that text or refusal. For non-streamed calls, the complete provider response, including audio, remains available in `result.rawResponses[].providerData`. For streamed calls, consume source Chat Completions chunks from raw model stream events as they arrive; the reconstructed audio is retained for tracing, not in `result.rawResponses`. Null audio fragments are ignored. Malformed or non-cloneable audio deltas, or a stream that ends without audio data, fail with `ModelBehaviorError`. `toTextStream()` emits only assistant text. Use the [Realtime API](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/voice-agents) instead when an application needs low-latency, bidirectional audio.\\\\n\\\\n#### Responses WebSocket transport\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Responses WebSocket transport”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#responses-websocket-transport)\\\\n\\\\nWhen you use the OpenAI provider with the Responses API, you can send requests over a WebSocket transport instead of the default HTTP transport.\\\\n\\\\nEnable it globally with `setOpenAIResponsesTransport('websocket')`, or enable it per provider with `new OpenAIProvider({ useResponses: true, useResponsesWebSocket: true })`.\\\\n\\\\nYou do not need `withResponsesWebSocketSession(...)` or a custom `OpenAIProvider` just to use the WebSocket transport. If reconnecting for each run/request is acceptable, your existing `run()` / `Runner.run()` usage will continue to work after enabling `setOpenAIResponsesTransport('websocket')`.\\\\n\\\\nTransport selection follows model resolution:\\\\n\\\\n*   `setOpenAIResponsesTransport('websocket')` only affects string model names that are later resolved through the OpenAI provider while using the Responses API.\\\\n*   If you pass a concrete `Model` instance to an `Agent` or `Runner`, that instance is used as-is. `OpenAIResponsesWSModel` stays on WebSocket, `OpenAIResponsesModel` stays on HTTP, and `OpenAIChatCompletionsModel` stays on Chat Completions.\\\\n*   If you provide your own `modelProvider`, that provider controls model resolution. Enable WebSocket there instead of relying on the global setter.\\\\n*   If you route through a proxy, gateway, or other OpenAI-compatible endpoint, the target must support the WebSocket `/responses` endpoint. You may also need to set `websocketBaseURL` explicitly.\\\\n\\\\nUse `withResponsesWebSocketSession(...)` or a custom `OpenAIProvider` / `Runner` only when you want to optimize connection reuse and manage the websocket provider lifecycle more explicitly:\\\\n\\\\n*   `withResponsesWebSocketSession(...)`: convenient scoped lifecycle with automatic cleanup after the callback.\\\\n*   Custom `OpenAIProvider` / `Runner`: explicit lifecycle control (including shutdown cleanup) in your own app architecture.\\\\n\\\\nDespite the name, `withResponsesWebSocketSession(...)` is a transport lifecycle helper and is unrelated to the memory `Session` interface described in the [sessions guide](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/sessions).\\\\n\\\\nIf you use a websocket proxy or gateway, configure `websocketBaseURL` on `OpenAIProvider` or set `OPENAI_WEBSOCKET_BASE_URL`.\\\\n\\\\nIn `responsesWebSocketOptions`, `pingIntervalMs` sets the interval between client pings; omit it or set it to `null` to disable pings. `pingTimeoutMs` sets how long to wait for a pong before terminating or closing the socket; omit it or set it to `null` to disable the heartbeat timeout while leaving pings enabled. Keepalive requires a WebSocket implementation that exposes ping and pong support.\\\\n\\\\nIf you instantiate `OpenAIProvider` yourself, remember that websocket-backed Responses model wrappers are cached by default for connection reuse. Call `await provider.close()` during shutdown to release those cached connections. `withResponsesWebSocketSession(...)` exists largely to manage that lifecycle for you: it creates a websocket-enabled provider and runner, passes them to your callback, and always closes the provider afterward. Use `providerOptions` for the temporary provider and `runnerConfig` for callback-scoped runner defaults.\\\\n\\\\nSee [`examples/basic/stream-ws.ts`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/tree/main/examples/basic/stream-ws.ts) for a full streaming + HITL example using the Responses WebSocket transport.\\\\n\\\\n#### Responses-only deferred tool loading\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Responses-only deferred tool loading”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#responses-only-deferred-tool-loading)\\\\n\\\\n`toolSearchTool()`, `toolNamespace()`, and function tools or hosted MCP tools that set `deferLoading: true` require the OpenAI Responses API. The Chat Completions provider rejects namespaced or deferred function tools, and the AI SDK adapter does not support deferred Responses tool-loading flows. Use a Responses model directly when you need tool search.\\\\n\\\\nTool search is supported only on GPT-5.6 Sol and newer model releases that support it in the Responses API.\\\\n\\\\nWhen a run includes deferred tools, add `toolSearchTool()` to the same agent and keep `modelSettings.toolChoice` on `'auto'`. The SDK does not let you force the built-in `tool_search` tool or a deferred function tool by name because the model needs to decide when to load those definitions. See the [Tools guide](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/tools#deferred-tool-loading-with-tool-search) and the official [OpenAI tool search guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search) for the full setup.\\\\n\\\\n### Hosted Multi-agent (Experimental)\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Hosted Multi-agent (Experimental)”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#hosted-multi-agent-experimental)\\\\n\\\\nExperimental beta\\\\n\\\\nHosted Multi-agent uses beta Responses API item schemas and is available only through the experimental `@openai/agents-openai/experimental/hosted-multi-agent` export. The API and SDK surface may change.\\\\n\\\\nInstall the provider package and OpenAI client as direct dependencies because the example imports both packages directly:\\\\n\\\\nTerminal window\\\\n\\\\n`npm install @openai/agents-openai openai`\\\\n\\\\nHosted Multi-agent lets GPT-5.6 models create and coordinate a tree of subagents through the Responses API. This differs from [SDK handoffs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/handoffs/) and agents-as-tools: the application does not create local `Agent` objects for hosted subagents or schedule their work. The hosted root agent delegates work, the service coordinates the subagents, and `/root` synthesizes the final answer. See the official [Multi-agent guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-multi-agent) for the beta API behavior and supported models.\\\\n\\\\n#### Configure the experimental model\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Configure the experimental model”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#configure-the-experimental-model)\\\\n\\\\nConstruct `OpenAIHostedMultiAgentModel` explicitly and pass it to an SDK `Agent`. Constructing the model is the opt-in; there is no separate enabled flag.\\\\n\\\\nThe experimental model uses a persistent Responses WebSocket. Local function outputs are injected into the active hosted response with `response.inject`, so keep the same model instance for the entire run and close it when it is no longer needed.\\\\n\\\\nRun a hosted Multi-agent workflow\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport OpenAI from 'openai';import { Agent, run, tool } from '@openai/agents';import {  OpenAIHostedMultiAgentModel,  getHostedAgentMetadata,} from '@openai/agents-openai/experimental/hosted-multi-agent';import { z } from 'zod';\\\\nconst lookupProject = tool({  name: 'lookup_project',  description: 'Return details about a project.',  parameters: z.object({ project: z.string() }),  execute: async ({ project }, _context, details) => {    const caller = getHostedAgentMetadata(details);    console.log(`Tool called by ${caller?.agentName ?? 'unknown'}`);    return { project, status: 'on track' };  },});\\\\nconst model = new OpenAIHostedMultiAgentModel(new OpenAI(), 'gpt-5.6-sol', {  maxConcurrentSubagents: 3,});\\\\ntry {  const agent = new Agent({    name: 'Hosted coordinator',    model,    tools: [lookupProject],    instructions:      'Delegate project research to hosted subagents, wait for them, and synthesize the result.',  });\\\\n  const result = await run(agent, 'Compare projects alpha and beta.');  console.log(result.finalOutput);} finally {  await model.close();}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nFor streaming observability, including hosted collaboration records and subagent messages, see the [complete example](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/tree/main/examples/agent-patterns/hosted-multi-agent-beta.ts).\\\\n\\\\nOmit `maxConcurrentSubagents` to keep the service default, currently three. A supplied value must be a positive integer.\\\\n\\\\n#### Tool execution and attribution\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Tool execution and attribution”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#tool-execution-and-attribution)\\\\n\\\\nEvery hosted agent uses the request’s model and sees the same local tool definitions. When any hosted agent emits a normal `function_call`, the existing Agents SDK runner executes the application tool. The Responses API’s call ID is the routing token: the SDK injects the matching `function_call_output` into the active hosted response for the caller that requested it.\\\\n\\\\n`getHostedAgentMetadata(details)` reads the hosted agent name from a tool callback’s third argument. This metadata is useful for logs and application authorization, but it does not control routing. Do not dispatch a function result by agent name; preserve and use the call ID.\\\\n\\\\nTool arguments arrive from the service over the WebSocket, and tool outputs are injected back into the active hosted response. Keep sensitive-data policy, tool authorization, and approval checks in the application. If a tool has side effects, make it idempotent by call ID so an interrupted continuation cannot repeat the effect.\\\\n\\\\n#### Output and streaming behavior\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Output and streaming behavior”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#output-and-streaming-behavior)\\\\n\\\\nOnly the `/root` message whose phase is `final_answer` becomes ordinary assistant output and contributes to `finalOutput`. Function calls remain ordinary SDK tool calls so the runner can execute them, and stable Responses items such as reasoning and hosted tool calls keep their existing SDK representations. Subagent messages, root commentary, and hosted collaboration records stay on the active WebSocket response and are not added to SDK history.\\\\n\\\\nRaw streaming events remain available through `raw_model_stream_event`, including hosted records and subagent messages. High-level item streaming keeps stable Responses items while filtering beta-only collaboration records, and high-level text streaming contains only the root final answer. This keeps RunState and session history provider-neutral while preserving the complete hosted event stream for observability.\\\\n\\\\nConsume a streamed run through its terminal event. If the stream consumer stops early, the SDK closes the WebSocket and abandons the active hosted response; a later run starts a new hosted response instead of resuming the abandoned one.\\\\n\\\\n#### Current limitations\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Current limitations”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#current-limitations)\\\\n\\\\nThe experimental SDK model supports Responses WebSocket transport only. The beta Responses API also supports hosted Multi-agent over HTTP, but `OpenAIHostedMultiAgentModel` keeps one WebSocket open so the SDK runner can inject each local function output into the active response before continuing.\\\\n\\\\nContinuation state for an in-progress hosted response is held by the `OpenAIHostedMultiAgentModel` instance. The model can reconnect a closed WebSocket before injecting a pending function output, but approvals and interrupted tools must still be resumed with the same model instance and the same WebSocket transport headers and query. Recreating the model loses the continuation state. One model instance also supports only one active run at a time.\\\\n\\\\nTransport failures are replay-safe only when the SDK knows the request frame was not sent. Once the server may have received the frame, the SDK marks the error as unsafe to replay and does not automatically repeat the hosted turn. See [Model retries](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#model-retries) for the general retry policy.\\\\n\\\\nDo not combine this model with SDK handoffs, `reasoning.summary`, or `max_tool_calls`; these combinations fail before the request is sent. Server-side compaction thresholds configured with `modelSettings.contextManagement` remain supported, while explicit calls to the Responses compaction endpoint are outside this model’s lifecycle. You can continue using SDK handoffs and agents-as-tools with the stable `OpenAIResponsesModel`.\\\\n\\\\n* * *\\\\n\\\\n## Model behavior and prompts\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Model behavior and prompts”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#model-behavior-and-prompts)\\\\n\\\\n### ModelSettings\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “ModelSettings”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#modelsettings)\\\\n\\\\n`ModelSettings` mirrors the OpenAI parameters but is provider‑agnostic.\\\\n\\\\n| Field | Type | Notes |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| `temperature` | `number` | Creativity vs. determinism. |\\\\n| `topP` | `number` | Nucleus sampling. |\\\\n| `frequencyPenalty` | `number` | Penalise repeated tokens. |\\\\n| `presencePenalty` | `number` | Encourage new tokens. |\\\\n| `toolChoice` | `'auto' | 'required' | 'none' | string` | See [forcing tool use](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/agents#forcing-tool-use). On OpenAI Responses, `toolChoice: 'computer'` forces the GA built-in computer tool when available. |\\\\n| `parallelToolCalls` | `boolean` | Allow parallel function calls where supported. |\\\\n| `truncation` | `'auto' | 'disabled'` | Token truncation strategy. |\\\\n| `maxTokens` | `number` | Maximum tokens in the response. |\\\\n| `timeoutMs` | `number` | Cooperative timeout in milliseconds for each model request attempt. Must be finite, greater than `0`, and no greater than `2147483647`. |\\\\n| `store` | `boolean` | Persist the response for retrieval / RAG workflows. |\\\\n| `promptCacheRetention` | `'in-memory' | '24h' | null` | Controls the legacy maximum prompt-cache retention policy when supported. This is independent of `promptCacheOptions.ttl`. |\\\\n| `promptCacheOptions` | `{ mode?: 'implicit' | 'explicit'; ttl?: '30m' }` | Controls implicit or explicit prompt-cache breakpoints for GPT-5.6 and later models. |\\\\n| `contextManagement` | `ModelSettingsContextManagement` | Controls provider context management, such as server-side compaction. |\\\\n| `reasoning.effort` | `'none' | 'minimal' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max'` | Reasoning effort for supported gpt-5.x models. `max` is supported by GPT-5.6. |\\\\n| `reasoning.mode` | `'standard' | 'pro' | string` | Selects the reasoning execution mode. This setting requires the Responses API. |\\\\n| `reasoning.context` | `'auto' | 'current_turn' | 'all_turns' | null` | Controls which reasoning items are rendered back to the model on later turns. This setting requires the Responses API. |\\\\n| `reasoning.summary` | `'auto' | 'concise' | 'detailed'` | Controls how much reasoning summary the model returns. |\\\\n| `text.verbosity` | `'low' | 'medium' | 'high'` | Text verbosity for gpt-5.x etc. |\\\\n| `providerData` | `Record<string, any>` | Provider-specific passthrough options forwarded to the underlying model. |\\\\n| `preserveRawUsage` | `boolean` | Preserve a detached, JSON-compatible snapshot of provider usage before SDK normalization on each completed model response. Disabled by default. |\\\\n| `retry` | `ModelRetrySettings` | Runtime-only opt-in retry config. See [Model retries](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#model-retries). |\\\\n\\\\nAttach settings at either level:\\\\n\\\\nModel settings\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Runner, Agent } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nconst agent = new Agent({  name: 'Creative writer',  // ...  modelSettings: { temperature: 0.7, toolChoice: 'auto' },});\\\\n// or globallynew Runner({ modelSettings: { temperature: 0.3 } });\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`Runner`‑level settings override conflicting per-agent settings. Nested fields in `reasoning`, `text`, `promptCacheOptions`, and `retry` are merged across runner and agent settings unless you explicitly clear an inherited value with `undefined`.\\\\n\\\\nWhen `timeoutMs` expires, the SDK aborts the current model request attempt. If retry processing neither starts another attempt nor surfaces a different failure, the SDK raises [`ModelTimeoutError`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents-core/classes/modeltimeouterror). A run-level abort signal still cancels the whole run. If model retries are enabled, the retry policy evaluates the timeout like another failed attempt; the SDK retries only when that policy opts in and the request is safe to replay or the application explicitly approves an unsafe replay.\\\\n\\\\nSet `preserveRawUsage: true` when you need provider-specific usage fields or need to distinguish an omitted field from a normalized zero. OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions, and AI SDK-backed models support it for streaming and non-streaming runs. Preservation is best-effort: if a provider does not return usage or returns a value that cannot be safely copied as plain JSON-compatible data, `rawUsage` remains `undefined`. See [Raw responses](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#raw-responses) for how to access the preserved payload.\\\\n\\\\n#### GPT-5.6 reasoning and prompt-cache controls\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “GPT-5.6 reasoning and prompt-cache controls”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#gpt-56-reasoning-and-prompt-cache-controls)\\\\n\\\\nGPT-5.6 adds request-level reasoning modes and explicit prompt-cache breakpoints. `reasoning.mode` and `reasoning.context` are Responses-only settings. `OpenAIChatCompletionsModel` warns once and ignores them, or raises a `UserError` before the request when strict feature validation is enabled. `reasoning.effort` remains available on supported Chat Completions models.\\\\n\\\\n`promptCacheOptions` is forwarded by both the Responses and Chat Completions model paths. The default `implicit` mode lets OpenAI choose an automatic breakpoint in addition to any explicit breakpoints. Set `mode: 'explicit'` to use only content parts marked with `promptCacheBreakpoint: { mode: 'explicit' }`. The currently supported minimum cache lifetime is `30m`.\\\\n\\\\nConfigure GPT-5.6 request controls\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Agent, run } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nconst agent = new Agent({  name: 'Research assistant',  model: 'gpt-5.6',  modelSettings: {    reasoning: {      mode: 'pro',      effort: 'max',      context: 'all_turns',    },    promptCacheOptions: {      mode: 'explicit',      ttl: '30m',    },  },});\\\\nawait run(agent, [  {    role: 'user',    content: [      {        type: 'input_text',        text: 'Treat this research brief as a reusable prompt prefix.',        promptCacheBreakpoint: { mode: 'explicit' },      },      {        type: 'input_text',        text: 'Summarize the brief and identify its main risks.',      },    ],  },]);\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nExplicit breakpoints are supported on GPT-5.6 and later models. The supported content-part types and breakpoint limits vary by API; see the official [prompt cache breakpoint guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching#prompt-cache-breakpoints) for current details.\\\\n\\\\n### Model retries\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Model retries”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#model-retries)\\\\n\\\\nRetries are runtime-only and opt-in. The SDK does not retry model requests unless you configure `modelSettings.retry` and your policy returns a retry decision.\\\\n\\\\nOpt in to model retries\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Agent, Runner, retryPolicies } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nconst sharedRetry = {  maxRetries: 4,  backoff: {    initialDelayMs: 500,    maxDelayMs: 5_000,    multiplier: 2,    jitter: true,  },  policy: retryPolicies.any(    retryPolicies.providerSuggested(),    retryPolicies.retryAfter(),    retryPolicies.networkError(),    retryPolicies.httpStatus([408, 409, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]),  ),};\\\\nconst runner = new Runner({  modelSettings: {    retry: sharedRetry,  },});\\\\nconst agent = new Agent({  name: 'Assistant',  instructions: 'You are a concise assistant.',  modelSettings: {    retry: {      maxRetries: 2,      backoff: {        maxDelayMs: 2_000,      },    },  },});\\\\nawait runner.run(agent, 'Summarize exponential backoff in plain English.');\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`ModelRetrySettings` has three fields:\\\\n\\\\n| Field | Type | Notes |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| `maxRetries` | `number` | Number of retry attempts allowed after the initial request. |\\\\n| `backoff` | `{ initialDelayMs?, maxDelayMs?, multiplier?, jitter? }` | Default delay strategy when the policy retries without returning `delayMs`. `backoff.maxDelayMs` caps this computed backoff delay only; it does not cap explicit `delayMs` values returned by a policy or retry-after hints. |\\\\n| `policy` | `RetryPolicy` | Callback that decides whether to retry. This function is runtime-only and is not serialized into persisted run state. |\\\\n\\\\nA retry policy receives a `RetryPolicyContext` with:\\\\n\\\\n*   `attempt` and `maxRetries` so you can make attempt-aware decisions.\\\\n*   `stream` so you can branch between streamed and non-streamed behavior.\\\\n*   `error` for raw inspection.\\\\n*   `normalized` facts such as `statusCode`, `retryAfterMs`, `errorCode`, `isNetworkError`, and `isAbort`.\\\\n*   `providerAdvice` when the underlying model/provider can supply retry guidance.\\\\n*   `replaySafety`, `responseStarted`, and `statefulRequest` so application policy can inspect the runner’s stable replay classification without reinterpreting provider-specific errors.\\\\n\\\\nThe policy can return either:\\\\n\\\\n*   `true` / `false` for a simple retry decision.\\\\n*   `{ retry, delayMs?, reason?, approveUnsafeReplay? }` when you want to override the delay, attach a diagnostic reason for logging, or explicitly authorize a non-streaming replay that the provider marked unsafe.\\\\n\\\\nThe SDK exports ready-made helpers on `retryPolicies`:\\\\n\\\\n| Helper | Behavior |\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\n| `retryPolicies.never()` | Always opts out. |\\\\n| `retryPolicies.providerSuggested()` | Follows provider retry advice when available. |\\\\n| `retryPolicies.networkError()` | Matches transient transport/connectivity failures. |\\\\n| `retryPolicies.httpStatus([..])` | Matches selected HTTP status codes. |\\\\n| `retryPolicies.retryAfter()` | Retries only when a retry-after hint is available, using that hint as an explicit delay that is not capped by `backoff.maxDelayMs`. |\\\\n| `retryPolicies.any(...)` | Retries when any nested policy opts in. |\\\\n| `retryPolicies.all(...)` | Retries only when every nested policy opts in. |\\\\n\\\\nWhen you compose policies, `providerSuggested()` is the safest first building block because it preserves provider vetoes and replay-safety approvals when the provider can distinguish them.\\\\n\\\\n#### Safety boundaries\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Safety boundaries”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#safety-boundaries)\\\\n\\\\nSome failures are never retried automatically:\\\\n\\\\n*   Abort errors.\\\\n*   Streamed runs after any visible event or raw model event has already been emitted.\\\\n*   Provider advice that marks replay as unsafe.\\\\n\\\\nStateful follow-up requests using `previousResponseId` or `conversationId` are also treated more conservatively. For those requests, non-provider predicates such as `networkError()` or `httpStatus([500])` are not enough by themselves. The retry policy must include a replay-safe approval from the provider, typically via `retryPolicies.providerSuggested()`.\\\\n\\\\nAn application can override a provider’s unsafe classification for a non-streaming request by returning `{ retry: true, approveUnsafeReplay: true }`. This is an explicit acknowledgement that the earlier request may already have been accepted and that retrying can duplicate a response or other provider-side work. Use it only when your application can tolerate that outcome. It does not override abort handling, a streamed request that emitted an event, or an unsafe streamed replay. When you compose policies with `retryPolicies.any(...)` or `retryPolicies.all(...)`, the approval is preserved only when a returned decision explicitly sets `approveUnsafeReplay: true`.\\\\n\\\\n#### Runner and agent merge behavior\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Runner and agent merge behavior”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#runner-and-agent-merge-behavior)\\\\n\\\\n`retry` is deep-merged between runner-level and agent-level `modelSettings`:\\\\n\\\\n*   An agent can override only `retry.maxRetries` and still inherit the runner’s `policy`.\\\\n*   An agent can override only part of `retry.backoff` and keep sibling backoff fields from the runner.\\\\n*   If you need to remove an inherited `policy` or `backoff`, set that field to `undefined` explicitly.\\\\n\\\\nSee [`examples/basic/retry.ts`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/tree/main/examples/basic/retry.ts) and [`examples/ai-sdk/retry.ts`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/tree/main/examples/ai-sdk/retry.ts) for fuller examples with logging.\\\\n\\\\n* * *\\\\n\\\\n### Prompt\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Prompt”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#prompt)\\\\n\\\\nAgents can be configured with a `prompt` parameter, indicating a server-stored prompt configuration that should be used to control the Agent’s behavior. Currently, this option is only supported when you use the OpenAI [Responses API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses).\\\\n\\\\n`prompt` can be either a static object or a function that returns one at runtime. For the callback shape, see [Dynamic prompts](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/agents#dynamic-prompts).\\\\n\\\\n| Field | Type | Notes |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| `promptId` | `string` | Unique identifier for a prompt. |\\\\n| `version` | `string` | Version of the prompt you wish to use. |\\\\n| `variables` | `object` | A key/value pair of variables to substitute into the prompt. Values can be strings or content input types like text, images, or files. |\\\\n\\\\nAgent with prompt\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { parseArgs } from 'node:util';import { Agent, run } from '@openai/agents';\\\\n/*NOTE: This example will not work out of the box, because the default prompt ID will notbe available in your project.\\\\nTo use it, please:1. Go to https://platform.openai.com/chat/edit2. Create a new prompt variable, `poem_style`.3. Create a system prompt with the content:   Write a poem in {{poem_style}}4. Run the example with the `--prompt-id` flag.*/\\\\nconst DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID =  'pmpt_6965a984c7ac8194a8f4e79b00f838840118c1e58beb3332';const POEM_STYLES = ['limerick', 'haiku', 'ballad'];\\\\nfunction pickPoemStyle(): string {  return POEM_STYLES[Math.floor(Math.random() * POEM_STYLES.length)];}\\\\nasync function runDynamic(promptId: string) {  const poemStyle = pickPoemStyle();  console.log(`[debug] Dynamic poem_style: ${poemStyle}`);\\\\n  const agent = new Agent({    name: 'Assistant',    prompt: {      promptId,      version: '1',      variables: { poem_style: poemStyle },    },  });\\\\n  const result = await run(agent, 'Tell me about recursion in programming.');  console.log(result.finalOutput);}\\\\nasync function runStatic(promptId: string) {  const agent = new Agent({    name: 'Assistant',    prompt: {      promptId,      version: '1',      variables: { poem_style: 'limerick' },    },  });\\\\n  const result = await run(agent, 'Tell me about recursion in programming.');  console.log(result.finalOutput);}\\\\nasync function main() {  const args = parseArgs({    options: {      dynamic: { type: 'boolean', default: false },      'prompt-id': { type: 'string', default: DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID },    },  });\\\\n  const promptId = args.values['prompt-id'];  if (!promptId) {    console.error('Please provide a prompt ID via --prompt-id.');    process.exit(1);  }\\\\n  if (args.values.dynamic) {    await runDynamic(promptId);  } else {    await runStatic(promptId);  }}\\\\nmain().catch((error) => {  console.error(error);  process.exit(1);});\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nAny additional agent configuration, like tools or instructions, will override the values you may have configured in your stored prompt.\\\\n\\\\nWhen a stored prompt already defines the model, the SDK does not send the agent’s default model unless you explicitly override it. That matters for `computerTool()`: prompt-managed runs keep the legacy preview wire shape by default for compatibility. To opt into the GA Responses computer tool on a prompt-managed run, explicitly set `modelSettings.toolChoice: 'computer'` or send an explicit model such as [`gpt-5.6-sol`](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol). See [Tools](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/tools#computer-tool-specifics) for the surrounding computer-use details.\\\\n\\\\n* * *\\\\n\\\\n## Advanced providers and observability\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Advanced providers and observability”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#advanced-providers-and-observability)\\\\n\\\\n### Custom model providers\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Custom model providers”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#custom-model-providers)\\\\n\\\\nImplementing your own provider is straightforward – implement `ModelProvider` and `Model` and pass the provider to the `Runner` constructor:\\\\n\\\\nMinimal custom provider\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport {  ModelProvider,  Model,  ModelRequest,  ModelResponse,  ResponseStreamEvent,} from '@openai/agents-core';\\\\nimport { Agent, Runner } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nclass EchoModel implements Model {  name: string;  constructor() {    this.name = 'Echo';  }  async getResponse(request: ModelRequest): Promise<ModelResponse> {    return {      usage: {},      output: [{ role: 'assistant', content: request.input as string }],    } as any;  }  async *getStreamedResponse(    _request: ModelRequest,  ): AsyncIterable<ResponseStreamEvent> {    yield {      type: 'response.completed',      response: { output: [], usage: {} },    } as any;  }}\\\\nclass EchoProvider implements ModelProvider {  getModel(_modelName?: string): Promise<Model> | Model {    return new EchoModel();  }}\\\\nconst runner = new Runner({ modelProvider: new EchoProvider() });console.log(runner.config.modelProvider.getModel());const agent = new Agent({  name: 'Test Agent',  instructions: 'You are a helpful assistant.',  model: new EchoModel(),  modelSettings: { temperature: 0.7, toolChoice: 'auto' },});console.log(agent.model);\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nIf you want every `run()` call and every newly constructed `Runner` to use the same provider by default, set it once during app startup:\\\\n\\\\nSet a default model provider\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { setDefaultModelProvider } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nsetDefaultModelProvider({  async getModel() {    // Return any Model implementation here.    throw new Error('Provide your own model implementation.');  },});\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThis is useful when your app standardizes on a non-OpenAI provider and you do not want to pass a custom `Runner` everywhere.\\\\n\\\\n#### AI SDK integration\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “AI SDK integration”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#ai-sdk-integration)\\\\n\\\\nIf you want to use non-OpenAI models without implementing `ModelProvider` yourself, see [Using any model with Vercel’s AI SDK](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/extensions/ai-sdk). That adapter lets you plug an AI SDK model into the Agents runtime directly, which is useful when your app already standardizes on AI SDK providers or you want access to the wider provider ecosystem. It also documents how Agents SDK `providerData` maps to AI SDK `providerMetadata`, plus the stream helpers available for AI SDK UI routes.\\\\n\\\\n* * *\\\\n\\\\n### Tracing credentials\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Tracing credentials”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/models#tracing-credentials)\\\\n\\\\nTracing is already enabled by default in supported server runtimes. Use `setTracingExportApiKey()` only when trace export should use a different credential than the default OpenAI API key:\\\\n\\\\nSet tracing export API key\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { setTracingExportApiKey } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nsetTracingExportApiKey('sk-...');\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThis sends traces to the [OpenAI dashboard](https://platform.openai.com/traces) using that credential. For exporter customization such as custom ingest endpoints or retry tuning, see the [Tracing guide](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/tracing#openai-tracing-exporter).\\\\n\\\\n* * run\\\",\\\"url\\\":\\\"https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"# Results\\\\n\\\\nWhen you [run your agent](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/running-agents), you will either receive a:\\\\n\\\\n*   [`RunResult`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runresult) if you call `run` without `stream: true`\\\\n*   [`StreamedRunResult`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/streamedrunresult) if you call `run` with `stream: true`. For details on streaming, also check the [streaming guide](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/streaming).\\\\n\\\\nBoth result types expose the same core result surfaces such as `finalOutput`, `newItems`, `interruptions`, and `state`. `StreamedRunResult` adds streaming controls like `completed`, `toStream()`, `toTextStream()`, and `currentAgent`.\\\\n\\\\n## Choose the right result surface\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Choose the right result surface”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#choose-the-right-result-surface)\\\\n\\\\nMost applications only need a few properties:\\\\n\\\\n| If you need… | Use |\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\n| The final answer to show the user | `finalOutput` |\\\\n| A replay-ready next-turn input with the full local transcript | `history` |\\\\n| Only the newly generated model-shaped items from this run | `output` |\\\\n| Rich run items with agent/tool/handoff metadata | `newItems` |\\\\n| The agent that should usually handle the next user turn | `lastAgent` or `activeAgent` |\\\\n| OpenAI Responses API chaining with `previousResponseId` | `lastResponseId` |\\\\n| Pending approvals and a resumable snapshot | `interruptions` and `state` |\\\\n| App context, approvals, usage, and nested agent-tool input | `runContext` |\\\\n| Metadata about the current nested `Agent.asTool()` invocation, for example inside `customOutputExtractor` | `agentToolInvocation` |\\\\n| Raw model calls or guardrail diagnostics | `rawResponses` and the guardrail result arrays |\\\\n\\\\n## Final output\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Final output”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#final-output)\\\\n\\\\nThe `finalOutput` property contains the final output of the last agent that ran. This result is either:\\\\n\\\\n*   `string` — default for any agent that has no `outputType` defined\\\\n*   `unknown` — if the agent has a JSON schema defined as output type. In this case the JSON was parsed but you still have to verify its type manually.\\\\n*   `z.infer<outputType>` — if the agent has a Zod schema defined as output type. The output will automatically be parsed against this schema.\\\\n*   The inferred validation output type — if the agent has a supported Standard Schema value defined as its output type. The output is parsed and validated synchronously against this schema.\\\\n*   `undefined` — if the agent did not produce an output (for example stopped before it could produce an output)\\\\n\\\\n`finalOutput` is also `undefined` while a streamed run is still in progress or when the run paused on an approval interruption before reaching a final output.\\\\n\\\\nIf you are using handoffs with different output types, you should use the `Agent.create()` method instead of the `new Agent()` constructor to create your agents.\\\\n\\\\nThis will enable the SDK to infer the output types across all possible handoffs and provide a union type for the `finalOutput` property.\\\\n\\\\nFor example:\\\\n\\\\nHandoff final output types\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Agent, run } from '@openai/agents';import { z } from 'zod';\\\\nconst refundAgent = new Agent({  name: 'Refund Agent',  instructions:    'You are a refund agent. You are responsible for refunding customers.',  outputType: z.object({    refundApproved: z.boolean(),  }),});\\\\nconst orderAgent = new Agent({  name: 'Order Agent',  instructions:    'You are an order agent. You are responsible for processing orders.',  outputType: z.object({    orderId: z.string(),  }),});\\\\nconst triageAgent = Agent.create({  name: 'Triage Agent',  instructions:    'You are a triage agent. You are responsible for triaging customer issues.',  handoffs: [refundAgent, orderAgent],});\\\\nconst result = await run(triageAgent, 'I need to a refund for my order');\\\\nconst output = result.finalOutput;// ^? { refundApproved: boolean } | { orderId: string } | string | undefined\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Input and output surfaces\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Input and output surfaces”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#input-and-output-surfaces)\\\\n\\\\nThese properties answer different questions:\\\\n\\\\n| Property | What it contains | Best for |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| `input` | The base input for this run. If a handoff input filter rewrote the history, this reflects the filtered input the run continued with. | Auditing what this run actually used as input |\\\\n| `output` | Only the model-shaped items generated in this run, without agent metadata. | Storing or replaying just the new model delta |\\\\n| `newItems` | Rich [`RunItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/type-aliases/runitem) wrappers with agent/tool/handoff metadata. | Logs, UIs, audits, and debugging |\\\\n| `history` | A replay-ready next-turn input built from `input + newItems`. | Manual chat loops and client-managed conversation state |\\\\n\\\\nIn practice:\\\\n\\\\n*   Use `history` when you are manually carrying the whole conversation in your application.\\\\n*   Use `output` when you already store prior history elsewhere and only want the new generated items from this run.\\\\n*   Use `newItems` when you need agent associations, tool outputs, handoff boundaries, or approval items.\\\\n*   If you are using `conversationId` or `previousResponseId`, you usually do not pass `history` back into `run()`. Instead, pass only the new user input and reuse the server-managed ID. See [Running agents](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/running-agents#state-and-conversation-management) for the full comparison.\\\\n\\\\n`history` is a convenient way to maintain a full history in a chat-like use case:\\\\n\\\\nHistory loop\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Agent, user, run } from '@openai/agents';import type { AgentInputItem } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nconst agent = new Agent({  name: 'Assistant',  instructions:    'You are a helpful assistant knowledgeable about recent AGI research.',});\\\\nlet history: AgentInputItem[] = [  // initial message  user('Are we there yet?'),];\\\\nfor (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {  // run 10 times  const result = await run(agent, history);\\\\n  // update the history to the new output  history = result.history;\\\\n  history.push(user('How about now?'));}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## New items\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “New items”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#new-items)\\\\n\\\\n`newItems` gives you the richest view of what happened during the run. Common item types are:\\\\n\\\\n*   [`RunMessageOutputItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runmessageoutputitem) for assistant messages.\\\\n*   [`RunInputItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runinputitem) for input admitted from `RunState.pendingInput` while resuming a run.\\\\n*   [`RunReasoningItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runreasoningitem) for reasoning items.\\\\n*   [`RunToolSearchCallItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runtoolsearchcallitem) and [`RunToolSearchOutputItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runtoolsearchoutputitem) for Responses tool-search requests and the loaded tool definitions they return.\\\\n*   [`RunToolCallItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runtoolcallitem) and [`RunToolCallOutputItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runtoolcalloutputitem) for tool calls and their results.\\\\n*   [`RunToolApprovalItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runtoolapprovalitem) for tool calls that paused for approval.\\\\n*   [`RunHandoffCallItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runhandoffcallitem) and [`RunHandoffOutputItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runhandoffoutputitem) for handoff requests and completed transfers.\\\\n\\\\nChoose `newItems` over `output` whenever you need to know which agent produced an item or whether it marks a tool, tool-search, handoff, or approval boundary. When you use `toolSearchTool()`, these tool-search items are the easiest way to inspect which deferred tools or namespaces were loaded before the normal tool call happened.\\\\n\\\\nIf a local tool or MCP server defines `customDataExtractor`, the corresponding `RunToolCallOutputItem.customData` contains the returned SDK-only metadata. This data is useful for application UI state such as renderer hints or internal IDs. It survives `RunState` serialization, but it is excluded from `history` and is not sent back to the model.\\\\n\\\\n`RunToolCallOutputItem.output` is the SDK-side tool return value. JSON-compatible primitives, arrays, and plain objects preserve their structure across `RunState` serialization. Other live values keep the existing string fallback. This wrapper value remains separate from `rawItem.output`, which is the model-visible tool output used by `history` and replay.\\\\n\\\\n## Continue or resume the conversation\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Continue or resume the conversation”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#continue-or-resume-the-conversation)\\\\n\\\\n### Active agent\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Active agent”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#active-agent)\\\\n\\\\nThe `lastAgent` property contains the last agent that ran. This is often the best agent to reuse for the next user turn after handoffs. `activeAgent` is an alias for the same value.\\\\n\\\\nIn streaming mode, `currentAgent` tells you which agent is currently active while the run is still in progress.\\\\n\\\\n### Interruptions and resumable state\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Interruptions and resumable state”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#interruptions-and-resumable-state)\\\\n\\\\nIf a tool needs approval, the run pauses and `interruptions` contains the pending [`RunToolApprovalItem`](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/openai/agents/classes/runtoolapprovalitem)s. This can include approvals raised by direct tools, by tools reached after a handoff, or by nested `agent.asTool()` runs.\\\\n\\\\nResolve approvals through `result.state.approve(...)` / `result.state.reject(...)`, then pass the same `state` back into `run()` to resume. You do not need to resolve every interruption at once. If you rerun after handling only some items, resolved calls can continue while unresolved ones stay pending and pause the run again.\\\\n\\\\nThe `state` property is the serializable snapshot behind the result. Use it for [human-in-the-loop](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/human-in-the-loop), retry flows, or any case where you need to resume a paused run later.\\\\n\\\\n### Server-managed continuation\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Server-managed continuation”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#server-managed-continuation)\\\\n\\\\n`lastResponseId` is the value to pass as `previousResponseId` on the next turn when you are using OpenAI Responses API chaining.\\\\n\\\\nIf you are already continuing the conversation with `history`, `session`, or `conversationId`, you usually do not need `lastResponseId`. If you need every raw model response from a multi-step run, inspect `rawResponses` instead.\\\\n\\\\n## Nested agent-tool metadata\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Nested agent-tool metadata”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#nested-agent-tool-metadata)\\\\n\\\\n`agentToolInvocation` is for nested `Agent.asTool()` results, especially when you are inside `customOutputExtractor` and want metadata about the current tool invocation. It is not a general “the whole run has finished” summary field.\\\\n\\\\nIn that nested context, `agentToolInvocation` exposes:\\\\n\\\\n*   `toolName`\\\\n*   `toolCallId`\\\\n*   `toolArguments`\\\\n\\\\nPair it with `result.runContext.toolInput` when you also need the structured input passed into that nested agent-tool run.\\\\n\\\\nOn normal top-level `run()` results this is usually `undefined`. The metadata is runtime-only and is not serialized into `RunState`. See [Agents as tools](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/tools#4-agents-as-tools) for the surrounding pattern.\\\\n\\\\n## Streamed results\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Streamed results”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#streamed-results)\\\\n\\\\n`StreamedRunResult` inherits the same result surfaces above, but adds streaming-specific controls:\\\\n\\\\n*   `toTextStream()` for assistant text only.\\\\n*   `toStream()` or `for await ... of stream` for the full event stream.\\\\n*   `completed` to wait until the run and all post-processing callbacks finish.\\\\n*   `error` and `cancelled` to inspect the terminal streaming state.\\\\n*   `currentAgent` to track the active agent mid-run.\\\\n*   `currentTurn` to inspect how many model turns have actually reached the request boundary.\\\\n*   `maxTurns` to inspect the limit applied to this streamed run (`null` means no limit).\\\\n\\\\n`currentTurn` increments only when a model request is admitted. A max-turn check or blocking input guardrail that prevents the request does not increment it, and a resumed run starts from the count preserved in its `RunState`.\\\\n\\\\nIf you need the settled final state of a streamed run, wait for `completed` before reading `finalOutput`, `history`, `interruptions`, or other summary properties. For event-by-event handling, see the [streaming guide](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/streaming).\\\\n\\\\nIf a streamed run is cancelled, `completed` still resolves after cleanup and `cancelled` becomes `true`, but turn-end fields such as `finalOutput` can remain unset because the current turn never finished. Resume that unfinished turn with `result.state` (and the same `session`, if you use one) instead of appending a fresh user message.\\\\n\\\\n## Diagnostics and advanced fields\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Diagnostics and advanced fields”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#diagnostics-and-advanced-fields)\\\\n\\\\n### Run context\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Run context”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#run-context)\\\\n\\\\nThe `runContext` property is the supported public view of the run context on the result. `result.runContext.context` is your app context, and the same object also carries SDK-managed runtime metadata such as approvals, usage, and nested `toolInput`. See [Context](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/context) for the full shape.\\\\n\\\\n### Raw responses\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Raw responses”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#raw-responses)\\\\n\\\\n`rawResponses` contains the raw model responses collected during the run. Multi-step runs can produce more than one response, for example across handoffs or repeated tool/model cycles.\\\\n\\\\nIf an output guardrail rejects a terminal function-tool result, the SDK sanitizes the current response in `rawResponses` together with the other SDK-owned replay surfaces. Do not rely on rejected terminal tool output remaining inspectable through this property. See [Rejected terminal tool outputs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/guardrails#rejected-terminal-tool-outputs) for the redaction boundary and limitations.\\\\n\\\\nEach response can also include `requestId`, the provider’s request identifier when one is available. The OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions models populate it for streamed and non-streamed HTTP requests; treat it as optional because some providers and transports do not expose one.\\\\n\\\\nFor Chat Completions text output, inspect the normalized `output_text` part’s `providerData.annotations` to read URL citations. Non-streamed responses preserve the provider’s message annotations. Streamed responses retain valid `url_citation` annotations received with text, deduplicate repeated citations, and ignore malformed or unsupported annotation shapes.\\\\n\\\\nFor Chat Completions audio, the normalized model response represents an audio-only assistant message with an `audio` content part. When that message becomes a run item, inspect the `RunMessageOutputItem.rawItem` for the same part. If a non-streamed response contains text or a refusal together with audio, the normalized assistant message keeps the text or refusal, while the complete provider response remains available in `rawResponses[].providerData`. For streamed mixed output, inspect raw model stream events when you need provider audio chunks as they arrive; the completed `rawResponses` entry contains the normalized text or refusal but not the reconstructed audio. The streaming `toTextStream()` helper emits only text.\\\\n\\\\nWhen `modelSettings.preserveRawUsage` is `true`, each completed response can also expose `rawUsage`, a detached, JSON-compatible snapshot captured before SDK normalization. The normalized `Usage` remains available as `response.usage`; `rawUsage` preserves provider-specific field names and omitted-versus-explicit values where supplied. It can be `undefined` if the provider omits usage or the payload cannot be safely copied. `rawUsage` is runtime-only and is intentionally omitted from serialized `RunState`, so copy any fields you need before persisting and resuming a run.\\\\n\\\\n### Guardrail results\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Guardrail results”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#guardrail-results)\\\\n\\\\nThe `inputGuardrailResults` and `outputGuardrailResults` properties contain agent-level guardrail results. Tool guardrail results are exposed separately via `toolInputGuardrailResults` and `toolOutputGuardrailResults`.\\\\n\\\\nUse these arrays when you want to log guardrail decisions, inspect extra metadata returned by guardrail functions, or debug why a run was blocked.\\\\n\\\\nFor a rejected terminal function-tool result, the SDK intentionally sanitizes current-response guardrail metadata. In `outputGuardrailResults`, `agentOutput` becomes `Output withheld by an output guardrail.` and `outputInfo` is removed. Current `toolOutputGuardrailResults` retain their verdict but omit `outputInfo`, and a `rejectContent` result uses the same placeholder as its message. Earlier accepted historical results remain unchanged.\\\\n\\\\nIf one guardrail fails to execute, results from sibling guardrails that completed successfully remain in the run state. For streamed runs, inspect the result arrays after `completed` rejects; for non-streamed runs, the `GuardrailExecutionError` carries the same settled `state`.\\\\n\\\\n### Usage\\\\n\\\\n[Section titled “Usage”](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/results#usage)\\\\n\\\\nToken usage is aggregated in `result.state.usage`, which tracks request counts and token totals for the run. The same usage object is also available through `result.runContext.usage`. For streaming runs this data updates as responses arrive.\\\\n\\\\nA completed streamed or non-streamed Chat Completions call counts as one request even when the provider omits its usage object. In that case, token totals remain zero because the provider did not report them.\\\\n\\\\nRead usage from RunState\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nimport { Agent, run } from '@openai/agents';\\\\nconst agent = new Agent({  name: 'Usage Tracker',  instructions: 'Summarize the latest project update in one sentence.',});\\\\nconst result = await run(  agent,  'Summarize this: key customer feedback themes and the next product iteration.',);\\\\nconst usage = result.state.usage;console.log({  requests: usage.requests,  inputTokens: usage.inputTokens,  outputTokens: usage.outputTokens,  totalTokens: usage.totalTokens,});\\\\nif (usage.requestUsageEntries) {  for (const entry of usage.requestUsageEntries) {    console.log('request', {      endpoint: entry.endpoint,      inputTokens: entry.inputTokens,      outputTokens: entry.outputTokens,      totalTokens: entry.totalTokens,    });  }}\\\\n```\\\",\\\"publishedTime\\\":\\\"Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:08:58 GMT\\\",\\\"links\\\":{\\\"run
